title.en: Lesson 1. Gentle Advice: -는 게 좋겠다 / 좋아요

blocks.md:
When giving advice, a direct imperative (*“Go to the doctor!”* = 병원에 가세요!) can sometimes sound demanding.

To offer caring, gentle advice (*“It would be best to... / You had better...”*), native speakers use **-는 게 좋겠다** (or **-는 게 좋아요**):

- *“감기에 걸렸을 때는 푹 쉬**는 게 좋아요**.”* (When you catch a cold, it’s best to get plenty of rest.)

Attach **-는 게 좋겠다 / 좋아요** directly to any action verb stem!

items.tip: It would be best to rest at home today.
It’s good to drink warm water.
It would be good to bring an umbrella.

blocks.q: When a friend has a bad cold, which sentence sounds the warmest and most caring?
blocks.why: -는 게 좋겠어요 offers warm, non-demanding advice: 오늘은 푹 쉬는 게 좋겠어요.

blocks.meaning: Because it is cold, it is good to dress warmly.
blocks.why: Action verbs take -는 게 좋아요: 입- + -는 게 좋아요 = 입는 게 좋아요.

blocks.q: Put in order: "It would be best to get plenty of rest at home today."

blocks.wrong: 감기에 걸렸으니까 병원에 가은 게 좋겠어요.
answers: 감기에 걸렸으니까 병원에 가는 게 좋겠어요.
감기에 걸렸으니까 병원에 가는 게 좋겠어요
blocks.hint: Action verbs take -는 게: 가- + -는 게 = 가는 게
blocks.why: Action verbs attach -는 게: 병원에 가는 게 좋겠어요.

blocks.q: It would be good to rest at home today.
blocks.hint: 오늘은, 집에서 쉬다 → 쉬는 게 좋겠어요

blocks.say: 감기 걸렸을 때는 따뜻한 물을 마시는 게 좋아요.
blocks.q: Read aloud with a caring tone:

blocks.md:
To express a personal hope or wish (*“I wish that... / I hope that...”*), attach **-았/었으면 좋겠다**:

- *“주말에 날씨가 좋**았으면 좋겠어요**.”* (I hope the weather is nice this weekend.)
- *“빨리 나**았으면 좋겠어요**.”* (I hope you get well soon!)

It combines the past tense marker **-았/었-** with the conditional **-으면** (*“If it happened, it would be good”*).

head: Base Word
Wish Form (-았/었으면 좋겠어요)
Meaning
rows: I hope you get well soon
I wish I had a lot of money
I hope to go to Korea

items.tip: I hope the weather is nice on the weekend.
I hope I pass the exam.

blocks.q: How do you warmly tell a sick friend "I hope you recover soon!"? (빨리 낫다 = recover quickly)
blocks.why: 낫다 is a ㅅ-irregular verb (ㅅ drops before vowel): 낫- + -았으면 = 나았으면 좋겠어요.

blocks.meaning: I hope the weather is nice this weekend.
blocks.why: 좋다 + -았으면 좋겠어요 = 좋았으면 좋겠어요 (I hope it is nice).

blocks.q: Put in order: "I hope the weather is good this weekend."

blocks.hint: Contract 오 + 았 into one syllable: 왔으면
blocks.why: 오 + 았 contracts to 왔: 비가 안 왔으면 좋겠어요. (비가 안 오면 좋겠어요 is also fine Korean, but this lesson practises -았/었으면 좋겠어요.)

blocks.q: I hope you get well soon.

blocks.md:
To express a hope or wish (*“I hope that...”* or *“I wish...”*), attach **-았/었으면 좋겠어요** to verb and adjective stems. Even though it looks like past tense (**-았/었-**), it expresses a **future wish**!

- Bright vowels (ㅏ, ㅗ) → **-았으면 좋겠어요** *(가다 → 갔으면, 좋다 → 좋았으면)*
- Dark vowels (others) → **-었으면 좋겠어요** *(먹다 → 먹었으면, 쉬다 → 쉬었으면)*
- 하다 verbs → **했으면 좋겠어요** *(합격하다 → 합격했으면)*

Be mindful of irregular verbs: ㄷ becomes ㄹ (**듣다 → 들었으면**), and ㅅ drops before a vowel (**낫다 → 나았으면**)!

items.ch: 주말에 비가 안 오고 맑았으면 좋겠어요.
items.tip: I hope it doesn't rain and is clear on the weekend.
I hope your cold gets better quickly.

blocks.q: You hope your friend hears good news. How do you say: "I hope you hear good news!"? (듣다 = to hear)
blocks.why: 듣다 is a ㄷ-irregular verb: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so 듣- + -었으면 좋겠어요 = 들었으면 좋겠어요.
오다 + -았으면 좋겠어요 contracts to 왔으면 좋겠어요.

blocks.q: 듣다 (to hear/listen) / Form the wish: 「내일 시험에서 좋은 소식을 ___ . (hope to hear)」
blocks.why: 듣다 is a ㄷ-irregular verb where ㄷ changes to ㄹ: 듣- + -었으면 = 들었으면 좋겠어요.

blocks.q: Put the words in order: "I hope my cold gets better quickly."
Which sentence expresses a wish for exam success?
options: 이번 시험에 꼭 합격하면 안 돼요.
blocks.why: 합격하다 + -했으면 좋겠어요 = 합격했으면 좋겠어요 expresses a hopeful wish to pass the exam.

title.ko: 4강. 헷갈리는 짝과 가르기: 권유 vs 바람 vs 의무
title.en: Lesson 4. Choosing Tone: Advice vs Wishes vs Obligation

blocks.h: Advice (-는 게 좋다) vs Wishes (-았/었으면 좋겠다)
blocks.md:
Both patterns include **좋다**, but their functions are completely different!

1. **-는 게 좋아요 / 좋겠어요**, **Gentle Advice or Recommendation** (*“It would be best to...”* or *“You should...”*).
   - 감기에 걸렸으면 따뜻한 차를 마시**는 게 좋아요**.

2. **-았/었으면 좋겠어요**, **Personal Wish or Hope** (*“I hope that...”* or *“I wish...”*).
   - 주말에 비가 안 **왔으면 좋겠어요**.

3. **-아야/어야 해요**, **Firm Obligation or Duty** (*“Must / Have to...”*).
   - 비행기 표를 오늘 예약**해야 해요**.

head: Pattern
Meaning
When to Use
rows: Giving gentle advice to a friend or coworker
Expressing personal hopes about the future/weather
Stating rules, deadlines, or essential obligations

items.ch: 머리가 아프면 약을 먹는 게 좋아요.
items.tip: If your head hurts, it's best to take medicine. (Advice)

items.ch: 내일 시험 결과가 잘 나왔으면 좋겠어요.
items.tip: I hope the exam results come out well tomorrow. (Wish)
I must submit the assignment by tomorrow. (Obligation)

blocks.q: Your friend is coughing badly. Which sentence offers gentle, caring advice to go see a doctor?
blocks.why: -는 게 좋아요 gives thoughtful, polite advice: 병원에 가 보는 게 좋아요 (It would be good to visit a clinic).

blocks.sentence: 피곤할 때는 무리하지 말고 일찍 [자는 게 좋아요].
blocks.meaning: When tired, it's best not to push yourself and sleep early.
blocks.why: When recommending a helpful action to someone, use -는 게 좋아요.

blocks.q: 쉬다 (to rest) / Offer caring advice: 「몸이 안 좋으면 집에서 ___ . (better to rest)」
blocks.why: Attach -는 게 좋아요 to the verb stem 쉬- to advise resting: 쉬는 게 좋아요.

blocks.q: Which sentence expresses a hopeful wish about tomorrow's weather?
blocks.why: For uncontrollable future events like weather, use the wish pattern -았/었으면 좋겠어요: 따뜻했으면 좋겠어요.

blocks.q: Put the words in order: "When you have a fever, it's best to drink warm water."

blocks.say: 스트레스 받을 때는 좋아하는 음악을 듣는 게 좋아요.
